utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Due to the little time some Judges in this Chamber have to meet between the morning and the afternoon sessions, we have unfortunately a late start in this case. And, Madam Registrar, this case is ... ?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-03-69-T, the Prosecutor versus Jovica Stanisic and Franko Simatovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Knoops, I was informed that you wanted to raise a matter, procedural matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I think it was still confusing in the medical documents regarding the waiver because we received an absence from court due illness document in which the right to waive to be present in court is not actually crossed by the defendant --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: -- while the non-attendance document under question 4, the English version does say that Mr. Stanisic is willing to waive his right to attend court in person. It's my understanding that Mr. Stanisic is not waiving his right to attend court in person, and I personally will go tomorrow afternoon again to the UN Detention Unit to speak about these two documents because I believe there might be confusion in these two documents for the defendant. But it's my --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, the most important thing, this is of course a formality filled in. Most important for us to know is whether he waives his right or not; he has never done that until now. If there would be any change in his attitude, then we would certainly hear from you, Mr. Knoops.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Another matter, we also received -- apart from these two documents, we received the medical report of today. Have the parties any need to put any questions to Dr. Eekhof? No need to put questions to Dr. Eekhof. I would, however. Could we have a videolink with ... Good afternoon. Dr. Eekhof, can you -- I see that the microphone is switched off.

utterances.speaker: MR. EEKHOF
utterances.text: [Via videolink] [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We can see your mouth moving, but we don't hear you. Apparently the microphone is not on.

utterances.speaker: MR. EEKHOF
utterances.text: [Via videolink] And now? Can you hear me now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I can hear you now.

utterances.speaker: MR. EEKHOF
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Thank you for being stand-by. I have a very, very short question for you. Under paragraph 2 of today's report you state: "During my visit of Mr. Stanisic today, his mental state of mind was still agitated and depressed, although less than last Friday ..." Now, it's my recollection that your last report was of yesterday, which was a Monday. Is there any reason why you referred to Friday rather than to yesterday?

utterances.speaker: MR. EEKHOF
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Your Honour, there's a simple reason. I visit him daily, but I only report once weekly as asked by the Chamber. And at the moments where he has to appear in Court, I give an expert report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But yesterday we received a report, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. EEKHOF
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Yes, I gave a report yesterday too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and was he still agitated and depressed, although less than last Monday as well, or is the situation the same as --

utterances.speaker: MR. EEKHOF
utterances.text: [Via videolink] No, it's -- it is -- I referred to last Friday because on Thursday there was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EEKHOF
utterances.text: [Via videolink] -- an incident which upset him and agitated him. I saw him on Friday. He was very agitated and very active even in his agitation. Yesterday he was still very agitated. Today he seems to rest a bit in the situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for this further information. Dr. Eekhof, thank you for remaining stand-by. The Chamber will determine whether or not to proceed. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. EEKHOF
utterances.text: [Via videolink] You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We can close the videolink.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber decides on the basis of the report of this morning, Dr. Eekhof's additional information, that we can proceed in the absence of Mr. Stanisic. Next matter -- perhaps before the witness enters the courtroom, yesterday we ended in P18 with an invitation to the Prosecution, an invitation to both parties. Any results?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, we did have the opportunity to speak with the Defence, both Defence, concerning this exhibit. It's the Prosecution's position that the entire exhibit is relevant. It does contain statements of an alleged co-perpetrator of the joint criminal enterprise and discusses the activities and conversations with other alleged members of the joint criminal enterprise during the relevant period of indictment between 1991 and 1995. We believe that because of this relevance the entire exhibit should be admitted. With that being said, we did have the opportunity to speak with both Defence. We are not able at this time, I believe it's fair to say, to agree to the admission of the entire exhibit. We are willing to continue our conversations with the Defence to see if a substantial portion can be agreed upon, and then we would await any future instructions or decisions by the Chamber as to whether or not the Chamber would like a further submission from the Prosecution on this or would like to decide the matter based on its review of the material.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Knoops, is -- what Mr. Weber said, does that reflect the actual situation, that is, that you started discussions, there was no agreement on the matter, and may I take it then under those circumstances that the Stanisic Defence takes the same position as it took yesterday in relation to admission of the video in its entirety?

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We reviewed yesterday the transcripts, the 42-page transcripts, and we still believe there are many portions which were not dealt by the Prosecution in chief with this witness. So which are, in other words, outside the scope of the testimony of this witness. But having said so, we are willing to sit down with the Prosecution to look into the document again and find ways to come to an agreement on certain portions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Jovanovic, any further submissions in respect of this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, for the time being the same reasons I pointed out yesterday; however, in my conversation with the OTP we came close to a possible solution. The proposal that I submitted to the OTP is now expecting for me to submit in a written form together with the identification of some of the documents that I wish to tender and I wish for them to be admitted upon mutual agreement. I believe that we have made some progress, but at the time -- for the time being I can repeat my -- yesterday's position. It is possible that we might reach an agreement, and I'll try and identify as soon as possible the document that I would like to tender for admission, and I will inform the OTP thereof as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Jovanovic. The Chamber would like to assist the parties in where apparently no agreement yet has been reached and where apparently the positions are still a little bit apart. And I'd like to give some guidance on behalf of the Chamber to the parties. First a general observation. In general any kind of documents - and that would include videos - should be tendered in a meaningful way in court through witnesses who are able to comment on them. This allows for a proper contextualisation, without which the Chamber is left to determine the relevance and probative value primarily on the basis of the document alone. These considerations are especially pertinent for documents of a technical nature for which the relevance and probative value is not immediately apparent. So the general rule is through a witness. As far as tendering evidence from the bar table is concerned, this often does not allow for proper contextualisation, as we have it when admitted through a witness, which leaves the Chamber to determine the material's relevance and probative value on the basis of the proposed evidence alone. And in order to facilitate the admission process - and I'm now talking about admission of evidence from the bar table - the Chamber requests under those circumstances a joint submission of the parties whenever a document, and that would include a video or one document or a set of documents, is tendered without being presented through -- to a witness, the tendering party should then submit a document containing a short description of each exhibit as well as its relevance to the indictment and its probative value if that's not immediately obvious from the description itself. In case of bulky exhibits with particularly relevant portions, a reference to those portions is needed. You could ask, Why a joint submission? Well, the Chamber would also like to be informed in the joint submission of any comments and objections that the opposing party may have with regard to each of the tendered exhibits. And the tendering party should provide the Chamber with the disputed exhibits. You see, a more or less structured way of tendering into evidence material which is not or not directly related to a witness through which that evidence is presented. This is general guidance. I'll now give you a very short provisional analysis of what we found yesterday. And of course the Chamber has had now an opportunity to read the transcripts. What we see, as a matter of fact, is that in the first portion - and I think this goes until approximately page 19 - the focus seems to be mainly on Eastern Slavonia; whereas on page 19 we move to a totally different area, we move to Bosnia, Zvornik, relationship between Mr. Karadzic, Mr. Milosevic, we see a lot of things that are passing by. Now, that first portion, that is apparently a portion on which this witness can comment. To what extent exactly he can comment and where he cannot comment anymore is -- of course we could not deal with that on a line-by-line basis; we will take a rather general approach. What we also see in this first portion, and that's repeated in the second portion here and there as well, is relatively irrelevant portions such as the background of the interviewed person, when he was -- whether he has ever spent some time in jail, some rather personal dealings and evaluation of the importance of his own position in all kind of matters. Therefore, in the first portion we see some material which is relatively irrelevant. We see a certain portion where in this interview matters are dealt with on which the witness could comment. That would therefore be a portion which would be appropriately tendered through this witness. And then in the second part we find information on which, at least from what we've heard now, we hardly could expect the witness to give any comment on it. It seems not to be very meaningful to tender that through this witness. Now, of course, then Prosecution could seek to tender that from the bar table, but whether that's appropriately done here or whether it would be more appropriate to tender this through a witness who could tell us about what happened in Bosnia, who could tell us about what happened in Zvornik, and therefore provide the context which is needed in the preferred way to receive this evidence, that is, through a witness. So at this moment the Chamber does not finally express its views on whether -- well, let's say on from page 19, whether it would accept it if tendered from the bar table or whether it would insist on it being tendered through a witness. That is the result of a provisional analysis of this document. Now, what the Chamber would like the parties to do is that the Prosecution further will look at that portion of the video which is most likely to be considered appropriately admitted through this witness and then to see whether we need all of that or whether there's some portions which seem to be irrelevant. If an agreement could be reached on that with the Defence, that would be appreciated by the Chamber, it would assist the Chamber; if not, we'll hear what reduced video you'll tender, and the Chamber will decide whether it, whether all of it or part of it, will be admitted into evidence. Mr. Weber, is that clear to you?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much for the Chamber's guidance. If it's okay with the Chamber, we would be happy to discuss that first portion during the first recess and report back to the Chamber later today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then the - if there's no other matter at this moment to be discussed - the witness could be brought into the courtroom again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: From your answer, I take it that you could hear me in a language you understand. Mr. Savic, I would like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you gave yesterday at the beginning of your testimony, and you'll now be cross-examined by Mr. Jordash. Mr. Jordash is counsel for Mr. Stanisic. Mr. Jordash, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Savic.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Let me take you straight to the 10th of June, 1990. From what you've told us you were instrumental in setting up the SDS board in Vukovar; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And by August of 1990, am I correct that Mercep was the HDZ president in Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, not the president of the HDZ but the secretary of the Secretariat of National Defence, that's what its name was.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And there was, is this right, a violent take-over of the National Defence staff?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Just briefly, what was that about?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to tell you much because we did not participate in power. We were newly established party after the elections, and we did not hold any responsibility for any of the activities that were taking place within the power in that administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: So basically the HDZ were dominating all the positions, is that correct, in Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The HDZ took 16 per cent of the votes in the elections that took place in April, and then there was the second round in early May. However, after the elections the state started functioning as an HDZ state. So all the activities that were taking place at the time went along that line.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: So officials who were not part of that party were being forced to leave their positions; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And basically nationalisation was on the rise?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And the fragmentation between the Croatians and the Serbians was rising and widening; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you're referring to us locals, then that would be to a lesser extent because us locals -- we tried to maintain good relations. The pressure came from the side of Vinkovci and Osijek. We as locals were rather close. For example, a lot of my friends were HDZ members and people who were candidates were also HDZ members, and that fact did not have any influence on our relations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, may I just briefly intervene. I am not a native English speaker. Therefore, I'd like to be assured that we -- that I understand your language in the same way as you intend to speak it. You used the word "Croatians and Serbians." Now, from what I learned now, but I could be wrong, is that if we are referring to someone on the basis of his ethnicity not on the basis of to what state he belongs, that we then talk about Serbs, whereas about anything Serbian would be in relation to the state of Serbia. You used the word "Serbians" where I thought that you would, in my understanding, wanted to refer to Serbs, that is, to ethnical background of human beings. Now, if I'm wrong, I'd like to be corrected at this moment in my understanding of the English. If I'm not wrong, you're invited to use the words in the same way, that is, Croats for Croat ethnic background, Croatians for people holding Croatian nationality; Serb for someone Serbian ethnic background, and Serbian for linked to the state of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: It's -- I think the simple answer to that is that there isn't a simple answer, that the terms can be used interchangeably.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If that's the case, then we always have to clarify what we are meaning if it's interchangeably used. Perhaps not spend more time on it at this moment and try to find a way in court or out of court, perhaps with the assistance of our interpreters or CLSS, so to find a language that I always understand your words in the way you pronounce them.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I'll endeavour to make myself clearer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Am I correct, Mr. Savic, that by the summer of 1990 the members of the HDZ were arming themselves in the Vukovar --

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: -- region.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And this was visible for those who lived in that region, it was fairly public?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: This arming was of criminals and the unemployed, amongst others; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Everybody who --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Objection to the form of the question. It's vague to ask the witness broadly his own context of what he thinks criminals are --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's clear. The witness may answer the question. The objection is overruled. If you need any further clarification as what the witness understands from these terms, it can be asked from him. Could you please answer the question which was: "This arming was of criminals and the unemployed, amongst others," whether that is a correct statement.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All those who adopted new political views and joined them were armed, irrespective of their profession and the activities they engaged in at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And this arming also took place amongst those of Serb ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And in the summer of 1990 this arming was taking place through a black market in weapons; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And this situation went on for several months, is that correct, arming through the black market?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And what was this black market? Where were the weapons coming from? And how were they getting to the various ethnic groups?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that we had established our party and that our intention was to buffer all those things. I don't know how the weapons came, through what channels, but I took my distance from the weapons. We never wanted to fight fire with fire. We had other arguments on our side that we wanted to use.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, was this arming the kind of arming which led to old hunting rifles falling into the wrong hands? Was it that kind of black market?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was all sorts, but I don't know any details. I never had the time to look into any details. Whatever I did I did without taking weapons in my hands, only with my head on my shoulders, nothing else. I was never interested in weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, I am not accusing you of anything; if I do, then I'll make it clear. I'm just trying to find out what you know. Could I suggest to you that the weapons that you say you saw with Ilija Kojic were obtained by him through that black market? Could you give us your comment on that.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's just a supposition. I can suppose that. However, in my statement what I really wanted to say was that I wanted to ask Ilija not to use our people and not to put them in a difficult position as to how much weapons he was going to take and distribute, I wasn't interested in that. I apologise to you. I'm really taking up your time because I can't tell you anything specific about the arming because that was something that I wasn't involved in. I didn't want to burden myself with it. My style of work was completely different. It was completely public, transparent, and civilised, and that part of my work could perhaps be of assistance to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, at that moment I'm interested in the arming, but you've confirmed - is this right - that Kojic could have obtained those weapons through the black market? You say it's a supposition but you suppose that that could be right.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Because when you went to his flat - if what you say is right - you saw old weapons at his apartment; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Old weapons which were -- no, let me start this again. How many did you see approximately?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Five to six perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: So this was five to six old weapons at a flat owned by Kojic?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And yesterday you -- you gave evidence that Kojic had suggested to you that he'd received the weapons from Stanisic. Do you recall that evidence?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could you explain why a moment ago you were willing to accept that he could have accept -- got them from the black market, if indeed what you said yesterday was true?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once again I will repeat that I was not focused on weapons at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could I suggest to you, Mr. Witness, that Ilija Kojic never said to you that he'd received them from Stanisic.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You could.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, I do, and I suggest that that was a fabrication on your part, a late fabrication.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no need for me to make up things.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Let me ask if the witness could be given, please, a copy of his first statement dated the 16th of -- 16th to 17th of December, 2002, incorporating I think also 3rd, 4th, and 5th of February, ERN number 011G -- sorry, 0119-1905. I'm presuming that will come up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You would like to have it on the screen --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sorry, I beg your pardon. I'm just getting used to the facilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I think we'll need you to have a look at the B/C/S version. Now, Mr. Witness, I just want you to have a look at the front sheet there on the left side of the screen and just - if the screen could go up to reveal the signature on the bottom left - could you have a look at that. Is that your signature? Do you recognise that signature?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And you see the date of birth at the top. Is that your date of birth, the 2nd of February, 1949?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Perhaps the -- we could turn to the first page of the B/C/S, please. Perhaps the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I just want you, Mr. Witness, to have a look and check just quickly that you recognise this statement as your own.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Next page, please, of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Does that look familiar, Mr. Witness?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't know if you wish me to prove the statement more than I have. I'm in Your Honours' hands, or I can take him through very quickly the whole statement if it's the practice of the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: We have no objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay, Mr. -- Mr. Witness, I want you to turn to -- in the English version it's page 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And so what I want, if I can, is for the B/C/S version to be turned to around page 6, and I'm looking at the bottom of that where the sentence -- the paragraph that begins: "Around mid-1990 the distribution of weapons had already started ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Can you indicate when you've found that, Mr. Witness.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think it's on this page.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Let's go the next page, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Is that it, two-thirds of the way down the page with the "1990"?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm looking at this now.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay --

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. Let's just read through that paragraph quickly. "Around mid-1990 the distribution of weapons had already started. At first it was done under the cloak of the SDS party, but naturally that was done by the Serbian DB. For example, in Vukovar the man in charge was certain Ilija Kojic who was a police officer. I came to this information quite accidentally. One day Kojic came to look for me to my house in Vukovar, but since he did not find me, I visited him later in his apartment." Is that, Mr. Savic, what you told the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Reading on. "When I went there he asked me whether I needed any weapons. Naturally I rejected, since I was against weapons and I knew that the distribution of weapons was just going to bring trouble for the, let's call them, 'short-sighted people.' I also warned Kojic, since he was obviously connected to the weapons, not to connect the party with this distribution. Kojic was not a member of the SDS ..." Is that what you told the Prosecution, Mr. Savic?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And the bit I'm particularly interested in is the following sentence. "Since in Vukovar I was one of the most" -- sorry, "one of the prominent people who meant something, I was against violence. I conclude that Kojic must have had connections with the DB, since one cannot buy weapons at the market and there had to be -- there had to have been coordination with an institution." Is that what you told the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: So at that stage you were presuming DB connection; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And only later - I don't think we need to turn to it - but only later in your visits to the Prosecution of the 11th February, 2008, did you suddenly recall, if I can put it neutrally like that, that in fact Mr. Kojic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I apologise for interrupting Mr. Jordash. But just so we have a clear record, the date of the proofing note is the 11th of February, 2008; however, it is indicated in the first line that the interview was on the 20th of September, 2007. Sorry to interrupt.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I beg your pardon, sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: So basically five years after your first statement you meet the Prosecution, and then you recall that in fact Kojic had told you that it was Stanisic who had given you these five -- sorry, given him these five old weapons; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Can I explain?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first statement when I gave it, it was quite general. The topic wasn't really known. We talked and it lasted for five hours, a couple -- for five days, a couple of hours each day, and the statement was given in the form that you can see in front of you. As for other interviews, they were all centred on a certain topic so that essentially what was added had not been made up. Simply, if one concentrated better, if one put in effort, then one could be more certain in conveying what happened on a certain occasion. That is my explanation.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you for that explanation. Let's move on. Now, let's stay with this statement, the first statement we've just been looking at. You -- actually, before we move on to that next bit, your statement with the section we've just read, your general statement, as you term it, noted that the supply of weapons was first done through the SDS party. Is that correct? If you remember the first part of the paragraph: "At first it was done under the cloak of the SDS party ..."

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. That's how it was said, that the weapons were distributed under the aegis of SDS.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Right. And you were one of the key members of the SDS party at that time? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, I'm -- I'm not quite certain that we have no confusion here. We have two elements in that sentence. At first SDS and then -- but naturally that was done by the Serbian DB. Now, I took it from your question that you suggested to the witness that in the beginning it was the SDS, and that at a later stage it was that the weapons came from the -- that it was done by the Serbian DB. That was the suggestion in your question. The witness more or less confirmed what I find in his statement, and therefore I'd like to seek clarification. Was there -- was this involvement of the Serbian DB, had it been there on from the beginning, or did it start under the responsibility of the SDS, and only at a later stage that it developed in such a way that it actually became the Serbian DB? Or was the Serbian DB involved right from the beginning? Which of the two was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I will try to explain it in briefest possible terms. When the HDZ came to power, all policemen who were Serbs were talked by the Serbian DB to leave police force, to not accept the chequer-board flag, to not accept new employment. And the HDZ was pressing to remove as many people from the police force as possible. We had meetings with them trying to talk them into remaining, not leaving police force because it was important for them to remain there -- oh, I apologise, I spoke too much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me stop you there. I would like to focus on the distribution of weapons, whether on from the beginning the Serbian DB was involved in the background, although it may have looked as if it was the SDS, or whether only at a later stage where the SDS had started on its own that the Serbian DB became involved. That's the question, which of the two situations -- descriptions reflects the actual situation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So all the policemen who were left jobless or were leaving police force went to Serbia. I don't know what their fate was from then on. I suppose that one of their activities had to do with weapons. They were involved with weapons. I gave you an example of a situation where I was personally involved because I was asked by Kojic and things happened as I have explained to you. I have always tried to explain that the weapons were of less importance to us. We tried to avoid it as much as possible in our work so the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me stop you again. Your statement was: "Around mid-1990 the distribution of weapons had already started. At first it was done under the cloak of the SDS party, but naturally that was done by the Serbian DB ..." Now, was it on from the beginning done by the Serbian DB, or had there been a period in which the Serbian DB was not involved and where it actually was the SDS itself? Which of the two? And I don't need -- I just want to understand the line I read in your statement. Could you tell us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really did not follow the mechanisms and how that arrived. It arrived via people who were in the police, and it was done in the way as described in the statement. Everything relating to the weapons -- you have to understand that it was a new system, new system of power, new system in every aspect, and they were accepting everyone into police force. They were giving them weapons. And whatever we did was termed as an anti-terrorist activity, and whatever you did fell within some kind of a regulation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me stop you again. Who are "they" where you said "they were accepting everyone into the police force. They were giving them weapons"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Authorities, new Croatian authorities which came to power after the elections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, I still have got no answer to my question, my question being where you said that the distribution of weapons had started but -- although it looked as if it was the SDS, it naturally was done by the Serbian DB. Was that on from the beginning of the distribution of weapons, or was it initially the SDS involved and not the Serbian DB in the background? Or had the Serbian DB been involved all the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From the very beginning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: How do you know that, Mr. Witness? Are you not speculating on the basis that there were police officers leaving their jobs and they, in some cases, had weapons?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Do you know the distinction between the public service and the state service? The DB on the one hand and the public service on the other, do you know the distinction?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to define it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: So what you're --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, again your last question: "Are you not speculating on the basis that there were police officers leaving their jobs, and they, in some cases, had weapons?" The answer is: Yes. Yes to what? Are you not speculating? Yes, I'm not speculating. Or was it: Yes, I am speculating on the basis of the reason you gave. Or in some cases they had weapons? To what is the yes? But that is a result of the way in which you put the question to the witness. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Let me try to clarify things.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: This was a period, as you've told us, when Serbian police officers were losing their jobs in the Vukovar region; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: This was a period when police officers who were of Serbian ethnicity were leaving their jobs and in some cases taking their weapons with them; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, I can't be sure. I don't know. I simply don't know how the hand-over was done. It could be the way you described.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. So wasn't the arming of civilians, Serbians and -- Serbs, I should say, and Croats, done, as you've told us, through the black market in the first place?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Objection, compound. If we could please deal with this separately, the Croats as opposed to the Serbs, because I think there's been separate testimony in terms of the arming of those two populations. And he's given different answers to his knowledge base.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Matters become confused. Is it that Serb police officers kept their weapons and handed them over; and if so, to whom? Or is it that weapons came from any other source, black market, DB, you name it, and then were -- so we have now in our questions and answers apparently two distinct suggestions of flows of weapons going in one way or the other. We really have to clarify that by very precise questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: What is your evidence of weapons supplied by the DB? Is it your visit to Kojic?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, for me, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you. I'll leave it there for now. We'll come back to this subject, but for now that will be fine. I want to ask you now about your visit to JNA generals. Am I correct that you had a meeting with Nenezic, retired colonel-general during, 1990?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Am I correct that you met also at that same meeting Jovo Kokot a partisan general from Western Slavonia?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, those were not meetings. Those were my regular visits to him at his home. His door was always open to me, and I can tell you what the reasons for those meetings were.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to ask you some specific questions. Were those generals the link with the JNA in the field at that time, the field being in Slavonia?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Nenezic hails from a village between Vinkovci and Osijek, from Podrinje. He was certainly very close to his homeland and the -- and his activities and his presence was tied with the activities, but my reasons were not of that nature. He indeed was connected to some people, and he did things that he could and that he did, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And you also visited in 1990, having received a call, Milan Karadzic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Milun.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Milun.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And he took you to see some JNA leaders in the region; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And you were not in favour of what they were discussing or deciding to do; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: They were discussing what?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Karadzic invited me to a meeting. He told me where the meeting would be taking place, and he didn't mention anything about the subject. When I arrived there and when I saw the location and when I asked about the reasons, he said we were meeting with the military, and it was just talking about current situation, current problems, and that was a subject of every single meeting that took place at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, what were the generals discussing in relation to arming of a population?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The subject was very general. The situation was so and so, it was even worse than it is portrayed; we are monitoring the situation; we can resolve things within the next 24 hours. This was what was said. And then when it came to question time, and since I knew that they were in daily communication with them, and I had a question which I put very loud and clear. My question was what the role of the army would be in the future war which was uncertain. I alerted them to the fact that I would be speaking at the end of the meeting and that he we should forget everything because nothing was true of what was said. What would be the role of the army in the future war, and who would protect the Serbs in Croatia? Because they were the ones who always tried to portrayed their role as people who were protecting the Serbs. The response to that was as follows. They think that there won't be any war. And if there is a war, the military would be the buffer zone. And it was such a big word that they obviously took pride in using it, and they asked me whether I was happy with the answer. I said not only was I not happy, I was embittered because I perceived that as being considered an idiot if they give me such an answer. And who is it who told them that in a state where the army is supposed to be protecting the internal organisation and the borders of a state, that in such a state the military of that state could be playing the role of the United Nations.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And you accept this, don't you, that the JNA in fact took sides? By 1991 at least the JNA were fighting on behalf of the Serbs; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It wouldn't be a good explanation if the military was to protect the Serbs that had a majority in terms of the population of Yugoslavia. It was only the top military echelons, the leadership of the military, who could have provided a reasoning or an explanation to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. Let me ask you about a different subject for the moment. Let me take you to when you were arrested. Was that early April of 1991?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 31st of March, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And am I correct that, as a result of that arrest, and the news spread amongst the Serbs living in the area?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, it was not an arrest. This was how it was portrayed in the media to raise tensions. The action that took place in Plitvice - and Mr. Goran Hadzic and I spent the night there - that action took place in the early morning hours, and it was organised by the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Croatia. At 5.00 I was woken up --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Can I stop you. I want a specific -- time is short, so I'm just trying to focus you and me. As a result of the experience in which the Croatians detained you and Hadzic, passions in the area were inflamed, especially in Borovo Selo; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And local civilian Serbians -- Serbs started setting up barricades?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And arming themselves with black market weapons; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Let's suppose so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Old hunting rifles and the like?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It really depended on what people believed was an appropriate thing to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And it was around this time that the Seselj's men came into the region; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, may I take you back. You asked: "Old hunting rifles and the like?" The answer was: "It really depended on what people believed was an appropriate thing to do." I have great difficulties in understanding this to be an answer to what your question was, unless you'd say, Forget about the hunting rifles, let's move on. Otherwise you should seek clarification.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Did you hear His Honour's comment, Mr. Witness? Some -- let me put it -- let me break it down. Some people armed themselves with old hunting rifles and black market weapons; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Some people went to the barricades generally in fear but unarmed?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whatever you say about weapons, all I can offer is my speculations. For 24 hours I was in the car travelling around Western Slavonia or in that direction, in the direction of Baranja. I had back-to-back meetings. Do you really think that in a situation like that I was capable of giving weapons a single thought? The topic of armament was not on the agenda of any of our meetings, and there was no single meeting that I attended where I would allow anybody to raise that issue. If anybody did the meeting would be abruptly stopped. My main goal was Zagreb, talking to people in Zagreb, and establishing relations with Zagreb. Everything else paled against that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Moving away from where we were. Mr. Jordash asked you whether the Serbs started setting up barricades. Your answer was yes. Then he asked you about arming. Do you have any knowledge of the arms that were available to those who were at the barricades?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I learned about the barricades three days after I got home from the prison hospital in Zagreb -- Zagreb. I was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me immediately stop you there. So the answer is you don't have any personal knowledge about the weapons people had at the barricades, even you have only hearsay evidence on whether the Serbs starting setting up these barricades. You heard about it afterwards. That clarifies to some extent the matter. Please proceed, Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Let me ask you about something in your statement which you, I think, have told the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: If I could please have ERN number, this is the first statement again, ERN number 0119-1905 is what we looked at a moment ago. If you could find the paragraph with Kojic in it, I want the paragraph immediately below. If you look -- have you found it? It starts off with: "In Western Slavonia ..."

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Western Slavonia, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: "In Western Slavonia there were many military emissaries. For example, one of them was Jovo Kokot, a partisan general, who always used to travel in somebody else's company, like, for example, Jevrem Cokic who was the commander of the JNA Bjelovar garrison."

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: You told the Prosecution that?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, or some other military personnel who were active in the field.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Right. The Bjelovar garrison, where was that?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Bjelovar garrison is in the city of Bjelovar, in the direction of Zagreb, as you're leaving the city of Bjelovar on the right-hand side of the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you. This was a large garrison with thousands of JNA --

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And let me read on. "Since I did not agree with the cooperation, with the distribution of the weapons, but still people were keeping me informed, for example, I found out that at the end of February 1991 leaders of SDS were going to Belgrade to a meeting about organisation 1st of March, 1991, which was Pakrac's attack date ..." Now, I'm interested in --

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: -- your connection in this paragraph between Kokot, Cokic, and the cooperation and cooperation and distribution of weapons. Were you making that connection there?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had nothing whatsoever to do with General Kokot. General Kokot was an old partisan general, and he moved within his privileged circles for years. And we -- I had nothing whatsoever to do with him until he appeared at that meeting at Tolek [phoen] house.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: You did have connections with Jovo Kokot, you've already confirmed that to the Court. Can you -- is that right?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that meeting, yes. At the meeting, but the meeting had been arranged by Milun Karadzic, so Jovo Kokot was not somebody I had any previous connections with.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Am I correct that Kokot and other JNA generals within the SBWS region were responsible for distributing weapons around this time, around the time of 1991?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible -- well, I suppose that's how it was. They were military. There was some other more responsible people who came from Belgrade as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, let's just deal with JNA for the moment. Let's deal with the paragraph -- go two paragraphs down, please. "The person I had spoken to" -- we're dealing with -- I'm going to read the paragraph now. "The person I had spoken in Belgrade to was Veljko Dzakula, and to my surprise he was not against such initiatives." This, Mr. Witness, was the initiative of arming the population; am I right?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And, reading on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Objection. That's misstating the statement. That is immediate reference to the paragraph before it, which does not describe that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, as a matter of fact, are you objecting against the question or against the answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Objection to the characterisation in the question because it mis-characterises the witness's statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just -- if there's any objection against the way in which it is reflected, whether that's in a summary form or whether in its original, you're invited to verify that on the basis of a literal quote.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I will, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Let's go to the paragraph below before I deal with the paragraph I'm really interested in. It starts off with: "Dzakula and myself were talking about Pakrac, and he said that the time had come for the people to raise rebellion. And the only thing they needed, it was weapons." And that was --

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: That was the initiative that you disapproved of that Dzakula was taking.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me just explain. Veljko Dzakula was the president of the regional board of the Serbian Democratic Party. And every two or three days we met; none of our meetings were chance meetings. Veljko Dzakula had gone to Belgrade, and I learnt about that, to arrange an action - and this word "action" is a term that you can interpret any way - an action in Pakrac. And he did it of his own will. He decided to do that without any previous consultations with anybody else.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Let me ask you about the paragraph above that. You met Dzakula in Belgrade. That's what --

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And if we look halfway through that paragraph it says this: "When we met in Belgrade I remained with Dzakula until 4.00 in the morning. I was trying to convince Dzakula that no cooperation should be made in the distribution of weapons and in the cooperation with army and not to take part into the distribution of weapons ..." Is that correct? Is that what you told the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me just explain. I arrived in Belgrade, and I called Dzakula's wife who resided in Belgrade. Dzakula wasn't there, and I told her that I was staying at Metropol hotel, and whenever he returned up at home that he should head for Metropol hotel. That was the way things happened. There was a continuity there.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, let me just try to focus you and me. Were you warning or trying to warn Dzakula not to cooperate, firstly, in the distribution of weapons?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That came after when he arrived -- or rather, we started talking first, and then he informed me that he had agreed for Pakrac to vote for its unification with the municipality of Knin, that the police would vote for its unification with the MUP and that people would raise. And he also said, We will chase Ustasha from the MUP in their underpants. That was his explanation. And then after that came our conversation that you were referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, that -- thank you for the explanation, but you -- can you try to answer this simply. Were you against -- you were against Dzakula's initiative to distribute weapons, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And you were against his cooperation with the JNA because --

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And because that collaboration was about the distribution of weapons in part?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, I'm looking at the clock. Would this be a suitable moment for a break?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll have a break of 25 minutes. We'll resume at 20 minutes past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, you may proceed. Did you make any arrangements with Mr. Jovanovic about how to divide the time available to you?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes, I said I was going to try to finish within an hour, and my learned friend said he would try to finish by the end of the day. I think that was the best we'd got which came to finishing by the end of the day --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but -- but you've taken more than an hour -- at least if you look at clock time, it's different from net time. But let's not waste further time and proceed --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I'm going to go as quick as I can, for sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, let's try to focus and deal with the questions shortly if you can. Just finishing off the issue about the arming by the JNA, did Dzakula inform you that the plan was that the army would provide the weapons and they would proceed to then seize territory between Hungary and the motorway?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And this was early 1991, is that correct, when you were informed of this? Sorry, did you say yes or no?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you. And are you able to confirm this, that in the Vukovar region in 1991 the JNA had approximately 15.000 soldiers?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let's assume so if that's the information you have. It's just my assumption. I don't know this for a fact. However, the figure is high.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: The number of JNA soldiers in the region was in the thousands in 1991?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vukovar had very small barracks, and therefore the number is very high. It could just be a combination of the Osijek and Vukovar garrisons, the two together.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And are you able to confirm this that available to the JNA at that time was automatic weapons, machine-guns; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Rocket- and hand-held launchers?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had quartermasters, that is to say, cooks --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters didn't hear the last sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could you repeat the last sentence, Mr. Witness, please.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Vukovar we had quartermasters, cooks, and other auxiliary personnel. There was no combat unit there. So this is why I know nothing about how JNA units were armed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. I might have misled you earlier with the 15.000. Was there approximately 6.000 in the Vukovar region? Is that more likely to -- 6.000 JNA soldiers?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so. The barracks is really small, up to 1500 max.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Let me ask you this then: Are you -- do you have any information on the volunteers who came into the region? Am I correct that they were subordinated to the JNA or the TO in the region?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the period of time that we're dealing with, there were no volunteers. Once the war broke out the volunteers appeared, and they came both under Territorial Defence and under JNA depending on what interpretation people gave.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. So let's break this down a bit. In -- the volunteers started coming to the region at what point? Was this in 1991?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first volunteers appeared in Borovo Selo. As for the rest of the area, it was blocked, and there were no changes there. They appeared during combat which took place in late 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And were these the SRS volunteers who appeared in Borovo Selo, Seselj's men?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And am I correct that in fact the reason that they came into the region was that the TOs in the region were making official requests directly to the SRS in Belgrade, asking for volunteers?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about mechanisms that were used to arrange for the presence of volunteers.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: So you don't know why or how the SRS volunteers came into the region?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I suppose you know why, but you don't know as to who made them or sent them to Borovo Selo?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't even tell you why.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Let me just see if I can trigger your memory.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Can I have a look, please, on the screen at Exhibit 3906 -- ERN B/C/S 0116-9412.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Would you have a look at this exhibit, please, Mr. Witness, and have a quick read and see if you've seen it before or it reminds you of anything you recall.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see the document for the first time. I can see that it involves Podravska Slatina, which is Western Slavonia. It was sent to the Radical Party, Ohridska Street, the 12th of October, 1991. That's October.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, I'm suggesting, Mr. Witness, that this is the way in which SRS volunteers came into the region because military, TO, JNA leaders in --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you want to object to the question, then I'd rather first hear the question. And could the witness wait to answer the question once it has been completed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I'm suggesting that the way in which SRS volunteers came into the region was that local JNA or TO leaders, commanders, in - I want to keep it simple - local JNA or TO commanders made official requests directly to SRS Belgrade office, the war office in Belgrade; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Objection, foundation. If we could have some specificity as to what region we are talking about. For the past page we have just been talking about a general region. The witness has now identified a separate area in that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, I think it would be appropriate to lay some foundation, because the witness earlier said that he had no idea about the mechanisms, and you'd say you would trigger, not to refresh his memory, but apparently trigger his memory, which is -- well, let's see -- let's again ask the witness, having looked at this document, if anything comes back into his mind of which he has personal knowledge. Let's avoid that we invite the witness to do the exegeses of documents which is for the Chamber to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Let me -- if, Mr. Witness, you are unable to assist as to who sent or requested SRS volunteers to come into SBWS during 1991, then I won't ask you any further questions on that subject. Are you able to assist the Court on that subject?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We can see in the heading that it says SAO Western Slavonia, Krajina --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're invited to answer the question and not to start interpreting the letter. That's exactly what we'd like to avoid. So could you please answer the question that was put to you by Mr. Jordash. Whether you could assist us from your own knowledge as to who sent or requested SRS volunteers to come into SBWS during 1991. Have you any knowledge about it? Who asked? Who did send them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is obvious that it depended on one unit to the next, one town to the next. It was all individual. All of them had their own individual mechanisms. As for the area of Podravska Slatina which is mentioned here, I don't know anything about that region.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps the witness -- you tell us that it would be different from one unit to the next. Tell us about one unit. Who asked them to come, and who did send them? And tell us what unit you are talking about. And then we'll move to the next one which may be different.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll tell you this. First of all, this is a completely new territorial entity for me, SAO Krajina, Western Slavonia, I know nothing about that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm not asking you about this. You said it would be different from one unit to another, and you do not know anything about Podravska Slatina. Fine. You apparently know that it went not the same way for all units. Now, tell us what you do know, that is, give us one example of a unit who asked them, and who did send -- who asked for their appearance, and who did send them? You may choose whatever unit you have any personal knowledge about.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, then I'll choose Vukovar. I can only tell you about Vukovar. During that period of time there was the government of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem. If this is how calls were sent to the volunteers, then it means that the same would have been applied by the government of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem. But I don't know of a single document of a similar content that was sent from Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm not talking about documents at this moment. You said it was different from one unit to another. I just want to hear from you what you know about one example. Because if you say, This is different from that, then you apparently have some knowledge of the two, otherwise you couldn't compare them. Now, do you know of any unit, who requested that they would come, and who did send them? If you know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. During that period of time I was in Belgrade, at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, even if you're in Belgrade you sometimes can know something. But do you know, or do you not know? Because in Belgrade you can hear, for example, who requested --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You have no knowledge that. Let's then move on. Please proceed, Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Savic. Let me ask you -- I'm going to try to short-cut things. Let me ask you to turn to the first statement again, ERN number 0119-1905. And in the English version it's on page 15 -- sorry, let's go -- my page 16, and the paragraph I'm looking at is the paragraph which starts with: "I am not aware ..." There doesn't seem to be a B/C/S counterpart. Here we go. I'm looking at the paragraph at the top for Your Honours. "I am not aware that the SRS had a War Staff in Belgrade." Can you find that in the B/C/S version, Mr. Savic? Do you have that?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I can't see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Can you see it now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What portion would you like the witness to see?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: The English part is: "I'm not aware that the SRS had a War Staff in Belgrade ..."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: This is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's two paragraphs above the "weapons and political parties" heading.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I thought ...

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: This --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can see it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Just have a quick read of that paragraph, and let me ask some quick questions to try to shortcut things.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... answer these questions, yes or no? Ilija Petkovic was a member of the SDS board in Markusica; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Petkovic was also a member of Seselj's volunteer unit; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was commander of the War Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And am I also correct that Milan Lancuzanin, also known as Kameni, was the leader of the volunteers in Vukovar in 1991?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the questions are posed. It says Petkovic. And in the section of the statement, there's actually references to two different Petkovics. If we could please have the first name from the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, would you follow that suggestion.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes, I will.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Just going back to Petkovic, Mr. Savic. Ilija Petkovic was a member of the SDS board in Markusica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Milan Lancuzanin was the leader of the volunteers in Vukovar in 1991.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Was he a member of Seselj's SRS party?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Was he a member of the SDS or a SDS board?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: If you look at the paragraph below, the one we just looked at with Ilija Petkovic contained within it, and it says in the last two sentences: "In Western Slavonia Veljko Vukelic" was in charge of the TO --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Isn't it -- yes, we have to move to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I beg your pardon, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Witness, can you see the next sentence beginning: "I remember" --

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: The last two sentences: "In Western Slavonia Veljko Vukelic was in charge of the TO, and they agreed with the JNA and nothing could be done without the approval of the JNA." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: "Logistics, weapons, everything was under the control of the JNA." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: "This applied in all the areas." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Objection as to foundation. And if we could just have the time-period that's being referenced here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, apparently you took statements where time-periods are not addressed properly. Is that ...

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If we could just have the witness clarify what time-period is he talking about, this being run through the JNA.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I was going to get to that point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: This applied in all the areas. Which areas are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We spoke about Slavonia, Western Slavonia, and Baranja; however, things changed very quickly. At one point in time --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whether things changed depends on when they happened, and that's what Mr. Jordash will ask you questions about.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: When was it that the logistics, weapons, everything for the war that was now taking place, when was -- let me start that again. When was it that -- when the logistics, weapons, and everything was controlled by the JNA in the areas you've just mentioned?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until the conflict broke out.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: When do you put that?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As soon as Seselj's volunteers appeared, everything fell apart and everybody would put themselves under their command because they clearly said that they were against the JNA and they were under the control of the State Security Service.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: So just remind me, if you would, Seselj came at what point in 1991?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which area do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, when do you say everything changed? What was the date, the best you can do now?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once the conflict broke out and once the volunteers of the Serbian volunteer party appeared, everything changed. As events were taking place in different locations, they would go there. There isn't a specific date or something that we could point to.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, are we talking about 1991?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All of it is 1991, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Beginning, middle, or end of 1991 when Seselj came? When did it change in Vukovar, that the JNA were no longer in control of the logistics and supplies and so on?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I left Vukovar on the 2nd of May after the events in Borovo Selo. The left bank of the Danube had already been taken by the police, and the police had it under its control. Therefore, the arrival of all volunteers, mostly volunteers, went under the control of the police. If they didn't let somebody through, that person couldn't cross.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Isn't it the case that you were in Vukovar on the 18th of November, 1991?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was already November, end of combat. It's possible that I can't remember the date, but once the combat was over I came to Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, I'm suggesting that the combat wasn't over and you attended on the 18th of November. So could that be possible?
