Before the massacres -- there was a -- do you know of a meeting on the 18th of November involving Hadzic and a number of civilian authorities? Do you know of a meeting --

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean in Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: In Velepromet.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Velepromet that was towards the end of combat, yes -- or rather, I heard that there was a meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And am I correct that that meeting involved Prime Minister Hadzic?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Hadzic was there as was Arkan, Slavko Dokmanovic I think, and other people from the establishment.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And JNA leaders such as Colonel Vuzic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean Vuzic?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know the details. I am not clear about Vuzic. I don't know who that person is. But as for Arkan and for Goran, Slavko Dokmanovic, and I don't know who else, yes, they had a meeting. At the time I was at the staff in Sid.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And you're aware, aren't you, that on the 20th of November there were crimes committed by the JNA at the Vukovar Hospital, in collaboration with paramilitary groups; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: So we know, don't we, is this correct, in November 1991, at that point paramilitary groups are acting under the subordination of the JNA? Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And throughout 1991, I suggest, Seselj's volunteers, when they came into the region, were attached to various TOs and various JNA commanders, a unity of command; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Who was Seselj and his volunteers working with? Can you name the people who was working with or the group?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why would the military and volunteer -- units of volunteers have singled out Leva Supoderica as a special unit? And that would be your answer. Seselj's people were a special unit, the so-called Leva Supoderica headed by the so-called Kameni, Lancuzanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes. And Lancuzanin, I suggest, was subordinated with Seselj's volunteers with the 1st Assault Detachment, 1st Military District; is that right? Could that be right?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't confirm this. However, Leva Supoderica, as a special unit, was there in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. If you can't confirm that, then I'll leave it and ask another witness. Can you confirm this, that Soskocanin, who you referred to yesterday as getting shot, was he a TO commander at Borovo Selo in 1991?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was appointed by the newly establishment administration of SBWS as the commander of the Territorial Defence there.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: So he would have had access to the JNA supplies, wouldn't he?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That was the Territorial Defence of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem, as it was already known at the time. And if I may assist you with something --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Let me ask you this: Would he have had access to TO weapons and supplies -- local TO weapons and supplies?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let's assume so. He was its commander, so one would be able to assume so. But that's already -- that's again May 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the one hand we have November, and on the other hand we have May.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, what happens in November? What are you suggesting was the change in November?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were talking about the previous ratio of forces, Leva Supoderica on the one hand and others, I don't know. And if we're talking about Soskocanin, then we have to talk about the month of May, about a new ratio of forces on the ground. This is what I'm saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I'm not sure I followed that. Just briefly, in May of 1991 Soskocanin is the TO commander of Borovo Selo, and in November is he still a commander?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was assassinated on the 15th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: So what's the -- who takes over as commander?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Badza was the one. Radovan Stojicic, the assistant minister of state security of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: So you think he was the assistant minister of the state security? Are you sure about that?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No verbal response]

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could I suggest that he was a part of the public security, distinct from the state security? Do you know that distinction?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. I admit that I am not aware of the difference. In any case he was a high -- a police official of the Republic of Serbia, and he was appointed as commander of the Territorial Defence in Borovo Selo as such.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Mr. Savic. So when you use the term "state security," then you could be referring to the public security or the state security? You don't really make -- or are unable to make a distinction?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he didn't -- they did not make a clear line among themselves either. Their jobs intertwined, so it's really difficult for me to know because I think they didn't either.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Fair enough, Mr. Witness. Let me move quickly, and I'm going to try and finish the next -- the end in the next ten minutes or so, so I hope you can help me. Let me first of all turn quickly to your statement again. We look again, if you would, at the paragraph we looked at before dealing with Lancuzanin. Have you found that? Have you found that, Mr. Savic?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm looking. Yes, I've got it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. What I'm interested in is the sentence here, the first two sentences: "I remember that Ljubisa Petkovic was wearing a camouflage uniform. I do not recall whether he had some insignia on it. At one point Petkovic was replaced as commander of the volunteers and publicly accused by Seselj of being a DB agent ..." but this happened in 1993. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not remember the year; however, this was the schedule of events, the commander of a War Staff of a party. A party has a War Staff, if you will, and the commander is somebody from the state security, and that is the gist of the matter. Ljubisa Petkovic was a member of the state security --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And the point is this, that Seselj was unhappy about that because he believed Petkovic was working for the DB; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was a pure manipulation. Seselj was also working for the state security, but the moment when the manipulation took place is of no consequence.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, if that's your answer, we can move on from that. I want to ask you quickly about Arkan. You claim to have seen him in a restaurant and you say that he told you he worked for Stanisic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And why did you ask him the question? You said yesterday you wanted to make sure it was not Milosevic. What was the logic of that?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In order to -- Arkan put more questions to me than I to him. However, when we started that conversation, I followed my style. I always used to ask people very direct questions --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Mr. Witness --

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I simply asked him --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt you, but I'm trying to finish. Why did you ask him? Why were you keen, or why did you want to make sure he did not work for Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since the service as a service worked for Milosevic, it was really of no consequence who was whose boss there.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: So why did you ask him then, if it was of no consequence?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because it mattered. I explained to him why I'm talking to him. I told him that I understood what he was doing, I knew why he was doing it, but that our goals were completely different to put it simply.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Just request that the witness be allowed to finish his answer. They're open-ended questions, and the witness is attempting to provide a full answer for the next question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just. Yes, I would not under all circumstances, whether the witness is providing a full answer to the question, or whether he's providing a very full answer which is not totally unrelated to the question is now and then to be determined. The -- you may proceed, Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. Let me ask you a different question. You gave evidence yesterday that you'd seen Bogdanovic the day before seeing Arkan; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Bogdanovic had -- if you're telling the truth, Bogdanovic had said to you -- Bogdanovic had said to you, We gave you Arkan. So you knew from the day before that Arkan's boss was Bogdanovic. So why did you need to ask Arkan who his boss was the next day?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that at the time Bogdanovic did not really deal with that. In my mind Bogdanovic was a very reasonable man. I held him in very high esteem, and I thought that he was a person of high integrity. He was an MP and a president of a committee, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: That's right. He was -- he wasn't the minister of interior when you met him, was he?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at that point in time, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: But he was suggesting to you that he was in control of Arkan, wasn't he? That's what he was suggesting to you.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When he said, We have given you Arkan as commander, how I could interpret it. I believe that it was a decision that had been reached previously, that he was put abreast of that decision, and that he conveyed the message to me. I believe that this had been agreed previously while he was a member of the service, while he was involved in that. That's how I interpreted his words. That's how I understood him.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. If that's your answer. Could I suggest that you never had a conversation with Arkan in which Arkan said he had a boss called Stanisic. And that, frankly, is a fabrication.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had a meeting with Arkan upon his invitation, which means that I was not the one who called the meeting. I did not seek him. I did not call him. He wanted to have a word with me, we met, and things at the meeting transpired as I stated in my statement. And I can also give you a list of all of my other meetings with him. In any case, I never sought to meet him. I never called any meetings with him at my initiative.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. Let's ask, please, for your first statement again to come onto the screen, 0119-1905. And I want to turn to page 23 of the English version, and the second-to-last paragraph of the English version speaks of this meeting you had with Arkan. Could you find that in the B/C/S, please, Mr. Savic. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing's happening on my screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I think it's coming, Mr. Savic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could I just consult with my learned friend, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. Are we there?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: This was your --

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: This was your account five years ago. We can look at what you said then about the meeting with Arkan. "We greeted each other, and Arkan said to me: 'Brother, I turned out as being a thief and criminal to your eyes.' I said to him: 'A bigger thief and criminal is the one who told you that.' That was all we said."

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's how I'm reading it. Yes, that's what it says here.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: The point being: Nothing about Stanisic. That was a recent invention.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Here you can't see it. However, when I provided my first statement, that statement was provided in very general terms. And the person who recorded the interview -- the version that I provided is truthful, and the way my sentence was interrupted here, I can only assume that the person who was recording my words omitted some of my words. The recording clerk and myself looked at all the pages, but we did not pay attention to every detail on every page. And that is the only thing I can offer by way of explanation why the words have not been entered into the record of my interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: So if what you say is correct, then, you never said to the Prosecution, That was all we said. Logic dictates then the Prosecution must have put that in if you didn't. Are you saying that?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The ending of the statement doesn't make much sense to me. This last sentence is not making any sentence. It's not logical.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. Let's leave it at that. Could you just confirm that the first time you mentioned Arkan having the conversation where he told you he worked for Stanisic was on the 4th or 5th of July, 2009, when you spoke to the Prosecution --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I just want to be clear for the record. He has mentioned the conversation dating back to 2002, so if we could just be clear in the form of the question being asked as to what is being said.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. -- let me just -- yes, that seems -- it's again a composite question which creates possibly confusion. If you would please split it up.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Just -- Your Honour, I don't want to belabour the point. I just want to give you a chance to deal with it. You did mention the conversation with Arkan. In your first statement, you never mentioned him referring to Stanisic until the 4th or 5th of July of this year, did you?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be honest, I really don't remember when I was interviewed. However, the gist of all the interviews was the same. I can't remember exactly when I provided interviews and what exactly I said, but there's no single reason for me to add something or fabricate something. There -- if I were to go over the same grounds three times, I'm sure that I would change the sequence in my telling the story. It would never be the same, and that's the only explanation I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Fair enough. Let's move on. Two more short subjects. One is your references yesterday to Ilija Petrovic and Ilija Koncarevic. You mentioned yesterday that they were from the authorities in Belgrade, State Security Services, Milosevic, the Government of Serbia. Do you recall that evidence?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could I ask for statement -- it's the proofing note. ERN number 0632-1753, please. I beg your pardon. If you could just give me a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: If you look at the first page, the paragraph 4, this is -- reflects a meeting you had with Klaus Hoffmann from the Prosecution on the 11th of February -- sorry, it's a meeting you had on the 20th of September, 2007. And looking at paragraph 4, do you have it, Mr. Savic?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Now it says: "Koncarevic and Perovic" --

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Is that supposed to be Petrovic?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Petrovic, right.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: So I'll read it in that way. "Koncarevic and Petrovic were agents of the Serb military security ..." Is that what you told the Prosecution then, that they were agents of the military security, not the state security?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that is how it is stated here, then yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: That's -- is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question was whether you said it. There are two possibilities. Either that it's correctly reflected in this document, in that case you said it; or it's incorrectly reflected in this document, and that's then because you didn't say it. Did you say that Koncarevic and Petrovic were agents of the Serb military security?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, can I offer something by way of explanation, very briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I'd first like to have an answer to my question, and then if there's any need to further explain, I'd like to hear your explanation. But first, do you remember whether you said that these two persons were agents of the Serb military security?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then if there's any need for further explanation, I leave it to Mr. Jordash to ask you questions about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, my answer's yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And you understand the distinction between the military service and the state service? Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll try and explain. All was so intertwined. When Petrovic and Koncarevic introduced themselves, first they said that they were from Belgrade, from Milosevic, from the authorities, and you can interpret that any way you want. There was no major difference between the military and State Security Service -- or at least I did not see it. It was a combination or a mixture where both services were so interconnected it was not possible to make a distinction between the two of them. However, the fact is that whatever they did was the job of the state security, the establishment of the National Council, the establishment of powers, that would fall within the purview of the state security. And I agree, I accept, that what is stated herein is what I said at the time. Because they all hid behind each other, and it was such a melange, such a mixture that it was very difficult for me to make any distinctions, although I was involved and I spoke to them. I can only imagine how difficult it must be for you to make that distinction.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And difficult also to make the distinction between military police, and also public police as well I suspect; is that right? Yeah.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If an agent comes and if he knows that people will line up with the military, then they say, We are from the military service. If somebody comes and knows that people don't want to line up with the army, they say, We are from the state security. If we go back to the period where all that happened and when you fast-forward and see how things ended, you will see that all of that is the consequence of all the combinations and all the things that they did hiding behind each other. The commander of the military district was running after Arkan and staging all sorts of shows together with him, the shows which would have been funny if they were not tragic. When we're talking about those times and everything that was happening at the time, it's really difficult to know who was who. They said one thing and did another. The only thing that was under control was people being victimised and plundered and property looted. Everything else was of no consequence at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Right. And on the same subject, I mean you met Dragan --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, so we are now approximately 25 minutes, I think, past the time where you said that you would finish in ten minutes. I notice that you consulted with Mr. Jovanovic. We need to have a break soon. Will you finish within the next couple of minutes or not? Otherwise we have to discuss how to proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I can finish in two minutes because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I'm looking at the clock. Two minutes means 5.30. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: On the same subject, you met Captain Dragan at some point in 1992; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 4th of August, 1992, when Captain Dragan was expelled from Knin, the first person who saw him and received him in Belgrade was me. I met with him in the office of Brana Crncevic at about 10.00. Brana said that Captain would come, and he himself was going to see Milosevic to see what to do about him. He arrived accompanied by Sasa Medakovic --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry, I'm against the clock, so I've got to cut you short. Can you confirm that Dragan said to you that he had not realised he was working in Golubic for the DB? Can you confirm that's what he said?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right now it's very hard. I would have to really make an effort to remember all that. But since I suppose that the office was bugged, I didn't really talk to him a lot. I let him do most of the talking, and I would occasionally put a question to him about the kind of work that he did over there and --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, it's a very straightforward question. Did Dragan say to you that he had been removed from Knin and he was not aware that he was being used by the Serbian DB, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think no. I don't think we even talked about those things.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, let's pull up the same statement, please, that was -- we had, the proofing notes. [Microphone not activated]. -- we can't. I'm referring -- well, maybe you'll accept it from me, Mr. Witness, that in the proofing notes from your time with Klaus Hoffmann on the 20th of September, 2007, that's what it says. Could you have said that to Klaus Hoffmann?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that's what it says in the statement, then, yes, I said that. But I would like to see it to remind myself of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Fair enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could the statement be pulled up, please --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If it would expedite things, the Prosecution would agree that the proofing note states: "Dragan had no clear idea why he was removed from Knin nor was he aware that he was being used by the Serbian DB ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Do you still wish to see it, Mr. Savic, or will you accept that we can -- you would still like to see it?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's my conclusion. That wasn't uttered by Captain Dragan. This is my conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Fair enough. Okay. Last question is this: Could I just suggest to you that you never had the conversation with Medic about Stanisic being his boss in the same way you didn't have it with Arkan and you didn't have it -- let me stick with Medic. You didn't have it with him, I suggest.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The conversation had to do with the context described in the statement. Slobodan Medic and I talked upon his invitation, and it was in the context described by me. And he also said that I should be in charge of that entire project. And I clearly stated that I didn't want to do that because I don't know whether they recorded this in the statement. I didn't want to create the government of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem and deal with agricultural land. Yes, it is true, we met and we had that type of conversation, just like with Arkan.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. Well, we'll agree to disagree.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Since Mr. Jordash just finished, I just wanted to raise one matter, exhibit --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In the presence of the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes. Exhibit 3906 was used with this witness. We did object to foundation just because it wasn't clear at the time of the witness's testimony; however, the Prosecution did inform Mr. Jordash that we would not oppose, and we would agree to the admission of the exhibit before today. So I didn't know if Mr. Jordash intended on tendering it, but I just wanted to let him know that if he does intend to, we would have no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I think that was the exhibit the witness didn't or wasn't able to comment on, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 3906 was the ... ?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The witness's own personal knowledge of it was limited; however, if counsel is seeking to tender it, we're not going to object to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and apparently you're not?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: No, not at this stage. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. So it's fine to know that you would have had an objection if it would have been tendered. That's useful information for the Chamber to think over during the next break. We'll have a break of 20 minutes, and we'll resume at five minutes to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Savic, you'll now be cross-examined by Mr. Jovanovic. Mr. Jovanovic is counsel for Mr. Simatovic. I take it that you have together calculated that there may be some time needed for re-examination as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it is with regret that I have to say that I will not be finished within the one hour that we still have remaining today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There is no way -- I left it to the parties to divide the time. Mr. Jordash consulted with you. Mr. Jordash, were you informed that by taking so much time that we would not finish the witness today. He would have to stay here for a week. I think I was quite clear at the beginning yesterday. It can be finished -- the witness we conclude for the testimony tomorrow? The answer was yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: There has been some delays. That's been the problem. And the way in which --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the guidance of the Chamber was 80 per cent to 100 per cent approximately from the time taken in chief. I can tell you that there were far more delays yesterday. So therefore, even if the Prosecution has taken slightly more time, I think, than announced, you certainly did far more than ... And I saw you halfway consulting. If there was any way that you would not conclude the testimony of this witness today, I should have been informed, this Chamber should have been informed about it, not just to say, Well, time is not something to talk about, is to be used. Mr. Jovanovic, I give you two seconds to consult with Mr. Jordash on the matter, but -- Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution anticipates only ten minutes for re-examination, no more. I believe we used two hours and nine minutes in examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Until now, two hours and nine minutes for the Office of the Prosecution. Defence until now one hour and 54 minutes. I think the guidance was quite clear, 80 to 100 per cent of the time taken in chief for both teams together. The Chamber is not -- of course we could say next time 50 per cent each, but we thought that where the matter was clear enough that you could -- you could divide the time, leave to Mr. Jordash if he has a greater interest in dealing with certain matters. The Chamber wants to -- one second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is 6.00. The Simatovic Defence has 50 minutes for further cross-examination, and then there will be eight minutes left for Mr. Weber. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Savic, you were shown the statement that you provided to the OTP in 2002, and you confirmed that the statement contains your signature; am I right?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please now look at the B/C/S version of your statement page 26, 27, and 28, the three last pages of the statement.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Could the counsel please refer to a 65 ter number.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The ERN 0119-1905-0119-1932. Could we have the B/C/S version starting with the title "miscellaneous." "Razno," R-a-z-n-o, page 26. Yes. Again the page is in English, not in B/C/S. Your Honour, will you allow me to read from the statement in order to save time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... it depends --

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now it's okay. Now we've got it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Savic, it says here -- or rather, what you said was interpreted as follows: "I decided to give my statement to the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia since it is obvious that I was involved in all events from the very beginning. It was completely clear to me that an arbitration for war crimes committed in these territories would require an institution of the international community. Therefore, the Court existed in my mind long before the International Tribunal was set up, and I decided to testify even at that time." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Am I right in saying that you embarked on providing the statement with all seriousness?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have page 28 containing the witness's signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Here it says that this statement was read back to you in the Serbian language and that it contains everything you said to the best of your knowledge and recollection; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness now please be shown page 3 in the same statement, page 3 in B/C/S, please. The next page, please. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Savic, the last two paragraphs on the page. It says in the statement in the penultimate passage: "The Chetniks followed Vojislav Seselj, the partisans Vuk Draskovic and war profiteers followed Zeljko Raznatovic, Arkan. Furthermore, since I had a lot of meetings and talks with people from the JNA, I arrived at a conclusion that the role of the JNA was to monitor the activities of the extremists and maintain peace. One cannot speak about the Chetnik Movement and militant forces without mentioning the role of the military security and the military because that was part of the authorities. That coordination was hidden, but it functioned really well obviously." Did you say that?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Page 4, please, paragraph 1. "It was never my intention to meet with representatives of the military, but they came to me, to talk to me. I had contacts with partisans and generals, for example, with Jovan Krkobadic who was a member of the Association of Serbs in Croatia, furthermore, with Radojica Nenezic, lieutenant-general retired, who hailed from Ada, a place between Vukovar and Osijek, as well as with Jovo Kokot who was a partisan general from Western Slavonia. They were some kind of advisor to the JNA and provided a link between the JNA and people in the field." Did you say that?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 7, please. Paragraph 4 from the top of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: "I asked Veljko Dzakula, asking for him to explain to me what the next step would be and what he meant when he said that people had to start an armed rebellion. It occurred to me to mention the use of arms when we're talking about a political solution. He said that the army would carry out its activities from the Hungarian border to the highway, whereby cutting off the Western and Eastern Slavonia from Zagreb and create a buffer zone of sorts." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: On the same page, the penultimate paragraph: "I had my spy in Western Slavonia, and I was aware of the meeting between the SDS and the JNA; however, normally it would be said that those were only briefings. Ilija Sasic and Veljko Dzakula attended the meetings regularly and Milun Karadzic occasionally, and the last person was the secretary of the SDS in Podravska Slatina. Those meetings started towards the end of 1990." Did you say that?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I know we're translating back from the B/C/S statement; however, just so we're clear his actual statement says "I had my informant" not "I had my spy," in the English version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, that seems to be a translation issue.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note that they do not have the English translation of the correct page on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Therefore whether the one is the correct translation, or the other one is still to be seen. But it's on the record now. We'll later deal with the way in which now the cross-examination takes place. Let's -- in order not to further lose time, Mr. Jovanovic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: On page 8, paragraph 1, it is stated: "Dzakula responded that everything was organised in Belgrade without any explanation as to who organised it. Dzakula said that the military would provide weapons and that they would take the territory between Hungary and the highway." Is that what you stated?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jovanovic, is my recollection wrong that this was read already to the witness at an earlier stage? Why read again to him and ask whether he said this, where it's my clear recollection that this portion was already read to him, if I'm not mistaken. Isn't it? Or is my recollection wrong?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, you're right, but I want to hear very specific answers from the witness because after providing his answers, he said that he was confused and he simply did not make a distinction between people who were in the field at the time and who worked for what service. And in this statement it seems that he stated everything very explicitly, and I'm just asking for him to repeat the same things in the same way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In other words, the statement that he provided originally does not contain any ambiguities.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: On page 10 below the title "National Council, Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem," second paragraph. "At the very outset when the party first was established, I tasked Soskocanin with establishing a group of 200 people who would provide the members of the party with security and prevent any provocations that might happen in such an environment." Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you indeed give order for 200 men --

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: -- to establish a group of 200 people who would provide security?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Page 12, the penultimate paragraph. "Jovo Ostojic across the Danube established communication that he, himself, controlled. He worked on behalf of the SRS, the Serbian Radical Party. He provided security for volunteers and arms who were being transferred from Vojvodina across the Danube." Did you say that?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Page 14. The title is: "Meetings with Seselj." Third paragraph. "Matic," I believe we are talking about Branislav Matic, Beli, "Matic was a member of the Serbian guard Vuk Draskovic, which was a parallel structure together with Arkan's Serbian Volunteer Guard." Did you say that?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Page 15, paragraph 1: "Let me explain Seselj's offer in the territory of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem, it was very difficult to establish any association without me. Kertes, Bogdanovic, Petrovic, Obradovic told me that personally, and the following party that was established in Krajina was the SRS, the Serbian Radical Party. But it was only in May 1992 with the great help of the RSK Army that had itself been set up by the JNA and by the government in Belgrade." And in this same paragraph it reads: "... the army was always actively involved in the elections in the Krajina." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: On the same page now, something that you've already spoken about - and I'm now asking for a more precise answer - you were talking about Ljubisa Petkovic, and you said that you met him in the Government of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: And that on that occasion he was wearing a camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: He was the chief of the War Staff of the Serbian Radical Party.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Page 16: "Weapons and political parties." "After the establishment of the SRS in Krajina in May 1992, Rade Leskovac was appointed the president of the SRS of Republika Srpska Krajina ..." And I'm not going to go on reading the whole thing. Just one thing from the same paragraph. "The army of the Republic of Serbian Krajina provided the SRS with financial support, logistics, weapons, and everything else. For example, people like Jovo Ostojic when they went to the front line in Bosnia they received weapons from the VRSK. It was a notorious fact, and on the other hand the SRS volunteers fought under the command of the VRSK ..." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Third paragraph, same page. "Holding a place number one, the first major distributor of weapons was the League of Communists Movement for Yugoslavia ... " Explain to us what is the League of Communists Movement for Yugoslavia, please.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The League of Communists Movement for Yugoslavia was a league of communists which was set up within the framework of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Who led that movement, that party?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it was General Mirkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In that same paragraph we have stated: "For instance, Ilija Sasic would receive weapons from them," this is a reference to the League of Communists Movement for Yugoslavia, "and the first volunteers were sent to Western Slavonia. The person who was in charge of the distribution of weapons in Western Slavonia was Nikola Kaloper ..." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just seek one point of clarification. I think a portion which was just read to the witness about the League of Communists Movement for Yugoslavia, I think the statement said that it was led by Mira Markovic, whereas now we find a name which is quite similar, although apparently another person, General Mirkovic. Was that a mistake at the time when Mira Markovic was mentioned or -- could you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the first designated chairman of the party was General Mirkovic. However, things changed so fast that we don't know how long whose tenure lasted, who did what, who had what role, what function, et cetera, so that it can be seen as --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was the movement at any later stage led by Mira Markovic or is that name a mistake?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That movement was in fact not established at all. Materials were distributed in the army for the setting up of the party, et cetera, but it all came to naught and youths sprang from it in fact later. So it is very hard to define where one began and the other ended, what was transformed into what from what. It will take 50 years of trials for that to be determined.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Jovanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: The last paragraph on this same page. "We both knew the retired JNA General Radojica Nenezic ..." I believe that you are referring to Ilija Sasic and yourself?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am referring to Nikola Kaloper.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 17, penultimate paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: "One day in July 1991 before the mentioned meeting in the League of Communists, the Movement for Yugoslavia, I met Kaloper in Nenezic's home in Dedinje, Belgrade. On that occasion Nenezic introduced Kaloper to me as his old friend and associate. The following day I was invited to see Kaloper in his office in the SKPJ building in Belgrade. You could only enter the building by producing your ID and a check as to who you were supposed to meet with there. In Kaloper's office I saw a large number of journalists who had escaped from Croatia and some people from Podravska Slatina ..." and then you mention a number of names. And then there is a sentence in that same paragraph. "On that occasion Kaloper told me that in Western and Eastern Slavonia, in the area of Vukovar and Osijek between 12 and 15.000 rifles had been distributed." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: On page 18, the first paragraph, you stated: "In order to reach Bobota one has to ferry across the Danube on a raft. Kaloper and General Nenezic were accompanied by the Novi Sad JNA Corps because Kaloper was reporting to Novi Sad Corps command, and General Bratic [phoen] who was the corps commander was in charge of transport and security ..." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On the same page, paragraph 3, third paragraph. "At a certain point Dusan Pekic a JNA general, was retired who was also the vice president of the association of Serbs from Croatia, who live in Serbia, in Belgrade, and Goran Hadzic's advisor for military issues. Dusan Pekic became the contact person in the association for people from Slavonia and Krajina who asked for weapons and support for war operations. Once in 1991 I saw outside the seat of the association Jovo Ostojic who was loading uniforms into a van. Dusan Pekic set up a centre for the training of volunteers in Prigrevica [phoen]. And Jovo Ostojic was the commander. The president of the association was Professor Vucinic, whose first name I do not know. And the secretary-general was Rodojkovic [phoen], a JNA retired general whose first name I do not know." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: In the next paragraph: "People from Knin joined the association at whose head was the mayor of Knin Milan Babic who was their president and mentor." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Page 19, second paragraph. "Pekic was one of the men who organised work in the field and who whole-heartedly supported Slobodan Milosevic ..." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Page 22 under the title: "Serbian Volunteers Guard and similar issues" -- and related issues. "It was from Radmilo Bogdanovic that I heard for the first time about the decision for Arkan to become the commander for Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem. This decision was taken by the Serbian parliament on the 15th of May, 1991 ..." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, something is incorrect. The date is not right. The 15th of May was the date when I was in parliament. No decisions were adopted nor had they anything to do with this.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: It was not adopted on that day, or it was not adopted at all?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is a typo. The 15th was the day when I was in parliament. No decisions were taken on that day, and it was the time when I found that he was coming out -- he was the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: But are you referring to an Assembly decision. Can I then conclude that that decision had been taken prior to the 15th of May when you were in Assembly?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe this is not a decision which is generally taken by parliament, and it has nothing to do with the 15th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I will ask you what I asked you in the beginning --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you take a break -- I would say if you take a breath, then you would allow our interpreters and our transcriber to take a breath as well. Would you take a breath now and then. Mr. Weber, you also want to take a breath?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. I just wanted to be clear the statement that's been quoted, it references no decision of the Serbian parliament. I believe this is being placed to the witness out of context. It's from -- on the English version page 22, it's underneath the section entitled "Serbian Volunteer Guard" in the very first sentence.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: There is a discrepancy between the translation and the original.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is -- you've heard the comments of the interpreters, that there is a discrepancy. Could you please slowly put the same issue to the witness again, Mr. Jovanovic. And may I ask, the statement was taken -- perhaps I should ask the witness. You were speaking your own language when you gave that statement; is that correct, Mr. Savic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So we are in a situation where the original is the English, and then it has been apparently re-read to him in his own language, which can create some discrepancies now and then. Would you please put again to the witness slowly the passage Mr. Weber referred to, Mr. Jovanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: "It was from Radmilo Bogdanovic that I first heard about the decision for Arkan to become commander for Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem. The decision was adopted by the Serbian parliament on the 15th of May, 1991 ..."

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A typo in my view because it is illogical. It is illogical to associate these two. First of all, this is not and should not be a parliamentary decision. This is not a matter decided by the Assembly, so this is a typo, and this is the only way in which I can interpret it. The sentence itself does not make sentence nor fits into the context.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Was this statement read out to you?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: When it was read out to you, did you notice what you are now calling a typo?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- testimony of the witness is clear. He has pointed at the logic of the whole matter and -- yes, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Just, the statement actually states not the decision happened on the 15th of May, 1991, it says in reference to when Radmilo Bogdanovic informed him of this decision, that this passage of information, the actual quote says: "This happened on the 15th of May, 1991, in the Serbian parliament." That's what the statement says.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So, therefore, you say that there is a -- could we ask the witness to look again at only those three lines in his statement.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm looking at them. It is not within the purview of the Assembly to adopt these decisions. The meeting was after 1700 hours, at which time the parliament adjourns. It works until 1700 hours. So we met after that time, after 1700 hours -- 1500 hours. I was there until 10.00, and there is -- it doesn't make any sense to make a connection between the Assembly and this. I can only treat it as a typo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jovanovic, apparently the witness does not confirm the accuracy of this part of his statement. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Savic, on several occasions when you adduced some new facts in relation to what you had said before, you said that you strained your brain, that you managed to remember some things. Can you remember the function, the office that Radmilo Bogdanovic held at that time within the Assembly? You did say that he was in charge of a committee.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it was the legislative or security committee.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: So the parliamentary security committee. You allow for that possibility?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do allow for that possibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Savic, to -- a question by my colleague. You said -- you replied in relation to an encounter between you, yourself, and Arkan in the Trozubac cafe in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: So in your statement you said what my colleague quoted, it ended with you saying, That was all that I said. And then subsequently when you were talking with the OTP some six or seven years later, namely, you recalled that you had also asked Arkan who he worked for.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: The Emigrant Society of Serbia that you worked for is in Nusiceva Street?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: And the Trozubac cafe is just outside the entrance to the Emigrant Society?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, just on the opposite side of the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: That was in May, this event was in May?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: At that time the cafe had an outside garden. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Where did you see Arkan, inside or outside?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Inside. There is a bar inside when one enters the cafe, and then there are some tables to the right-hand side, and that is where I saw him.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Inside?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, inside, in the cafe.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Please if you can recall, how big a space are we talking about inside Trozubac, the Trident cafe, and are there chairs and tables inside?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, there is a space around the bar. Now whether there were chairs or stools, we were not sitting in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: So Arkan was not sitting when you saw him inside?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he was standing at the bar -- he was at the bar, and we talked at the bar.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Was Arkan alone at the bar?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was not at the bar. He was in front of the bar. I believe that there was no one of his men -- in fact, I don't even know who the man was who brought me there, but we actually went out from the office, crossed the street, and entered the cafe.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: But did you used to sit outside that cafe when you went to the "matica," to the Emigrant Society?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, whenever I had time for a cup of coffee, I would be there, maybe outside in the garden, not inside.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: And Arkan used to come there also as a rule?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see him there for any time long or many times, but this was after I was released from the prison hospital in Plitvice and his arrival from Zagreb. So that that was recent, and we were linked in some sort of a context of those events.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know the owner of the Trozubac cafe?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, although people said that he was -- that it was in the -- in fact Arkan's cafe.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Had you heard that he was a friend of his who was the owner of the cafe?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the ownership was associated with Arkan. I believe that in a name it was -- the papers were in the name of somebody else, but it was a -- people said that it was Arkan's.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could anyone hear your conversation?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't paying attention. There was nothing missing or secretive. There was no need for us to be isolated from the rest of the place.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: So there was nothing secretive about the conversation in which you were asking Arkan whom you met for the first time, as far as I could understand you, who he was working for, and he answered you apparently that he was working for Jovica Stanisic. And you don't see anything secretive about that?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Other people could hear that?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why not? Whoever who was there. There was no mysticism, no secret, no secrecy about that conversation. It was a normal conversation that would have taken place with anybody else whom you've met for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: And now I'm going to ask you something about the meeting you had with Ilija Kojic. You've already spoken about that. Your meeting was in Vukovar. The weapons that he was talking about, did he offer them to you personally, or did he offer you weapons, a larger quantity of weapons?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he offered a piece to me personally. He said, You're moving about a lot. You have to be protected, and something along these lines. It was done in -- with the best of intentions. It was not a deal of any sort.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: So this was just for your personal security?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Not at all. Mr. Savic, did you know Trifun Ivkovic [phoen]?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: What was his function or position?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was working at the motel on the highway. I don't know what his position was, and after that he was the head of the prison in Sremska Mitrovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you sometimes go to the Sremska Mitrovica prison?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: What was the occasion?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't go to the prison. I went to the hotel which was also affiliated with the prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Why did you go?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To have coffee. On the way to Sabac where my mother lives I would often stop there, and I was in the office when he was the head of the prison there.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever go to Trifun's office when Croats from Vukovar were detained in the prison in Sremska Mitrovica?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not in the office. I was there one morning having coffee in the hotel, and there was a group of lawyers from Vukovar -- they were actually judges. I knew them all. And in the next room, the room behind, there was Trivo with some police officials. He took me into the room, introduced me to everybody there, and that's how the meeting ended.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I did not mean a visit to the prison in Sremska Mitrovica. Were you there at the time when Croats from Vukovar were detained in the prison?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean in the prison?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, in the prison.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never visited the prison at that time, never visited the prison, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Savic, do you know Emil Cakalic, the hygiene inspector from Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that he knows me better than I know him, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: So how did he get to know you?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He never really met me, Emil Cakalic, never did, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever interview him about the activities of the HDZ in Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Emil Cakalic was not even a member of the HDZ.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: However, this is what he's claiming. But did you ever interview him?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why would I interview Emil Cakalic when I had friends in the HDZ and I knew everything about want HDZ? I don't really know what I could be talking about with Emil Cakalic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever beat Mr. Cakalic?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would, with the agreement of the OTP, and we've already discussed that, I would like to show the witness a document that was disclosed by the OTP pursuant to Rule 68. I have it in hard copy, and I have left enough copies for the OTP, the Trial Chamber, and the interpreters. With your leave I would show the document to Mr. Savic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The fact that you have sufficient copies for the interpreters is an alarming message.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that you want to quote one or --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jovanovic. Yes, because you still have six minutes left, so reading the whole of the document would --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: There is no agreement from the OTP with respect to this exhibit. It has just been -- it was provided. We received notice that it may be used about five minutes before court started today. So we have not agreed to anything regarding the admissibility of this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Jovanovic said that he had discussed the matter with the agreement of the OTP, so he's seeking that agreement, he would like to show it to the witness. Is that well understood?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objection against putting it to the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: If I may interfere, Your Honours. The parties have agreed that if certain allegations are put to witnesses, the parties will not say what they base their allegations on. And I believe this is a case in that Mr. Jovanovic is not acting in accordance with to what he has agreed upon previously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This is a document, an Official Note, apparently not prepared for the proceedings before this Tribunal or -- no, apparently not. It was produced 16th of May, 1992. What would you like to do with the document, Mr. Jovanovic? I mean, this is a document, apparently an Official Note. An Official Note, from what I understand, are usually taken if someone is interviewed. What's the purpose of this document to be used at this moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is about the functions that the witness has held of which he's never spoken. He has testified before you about being the head of the SDS board in Vukovar and also that he was an employee of the Serbian emigration society in Belgrade. What is noted here in this Official Note speaks about his functions --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. If he had other functions, why not ask the witness whether he had those functions. I mean, if he has not spoken about it, I do not remember to have heard a question, Have you mentioned by now all the functions you ever performed? If there is anything you think that the information is not complete in relation to the functions he may have had, why not ask the witness? Even without the statement -- or you may find in this statement the relevant information for you. But let's first ask the witness, and then if then he says, I've never had any function, and if others say he had, then it would be time perhaps to look at the statement and say, But others have said you had. Could you just ask the witness about the functions you said he had never spoke before.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will ask the witness this.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever hold any functions that applied the duty to interview witnesses and abusing them in the process?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I now read just one paragraph from this Official Note to the witness, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and that would be on what page? Because you have now asked him. What page of the document?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The penultimate page in B/C/S as well as in English. The penultimate pages in both versions, the penultimate paragraph. Just one sentence is the last paragraph, and I would like to read to the witness the paragraph above that last sentence on the penultimate page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But perhaps first -- function which applied to duty to interview witnesses and abusing them in the process is something -- I never heard of such a duty, and I wonder whether this is a mistake or were you serious? I can imagine that someone would ask another person whether he abused someone, but whether he was performing a function that applied the duty to interview witnesses and abusing them in the process. The question is unclear to me. Let me say it this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I can rephrase. Did he de facto have the authority to act in that way?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you -- apparently, Mr. Savic -- a Mr. Emil Cakalic provided a statement which is referred to in an Official Note. In this Official Note he was reported to have said that on the 14th of December, 1991, that he was taken for questioning for the first time, and when he entered the room, he saw Goran Hadzic and Borivoje Savic. First question: Did you on the 14th of December, 1991, question Mr. Borivoje Savic [sic]?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I made a mistake. Whether you questioned Mr. Cakalic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I didn't. I have a very simple explanation. I've already discussed that with the authorities in Croatia. I've already discussed the issue with them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I just -- my first question was whether you questioned him, yes or no. Were you present on that date --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You were present not with him on that date in one room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I never ever, absolutely never interviewed anybody, and I can provide a simple explanation to avoid any further confusion in anybody's mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You've answered my question. Mr. Jovanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. My last question.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Savic, the invitation you received or the summons you received by the Croatian court, why were you summoned?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it was the war crimes court, I believe that's its name. First of all, Emil Cakalic and I provided two interviews about that to the newspaper of "Vecernji List."

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: You asked about -- I'm asking you about the summons. You've already answered the Judge's questions.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was summoned, and I explained what this was all about. My conclusion was that Emil was a professional witness, that he had been prepped and served on the platter to say what he did. And the Croats answered that Emil Cakalic had been prepared in The Hague, and that's where he had been told to say what he did, and that was the end of that story.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Savic. Very well.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to tender this document for admission as exhibit, and I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: We'd object to its admission. The authenticity of this exhibit -- the witness has not confirmed that these events ever occurred, or the reliability of the exhibit is also highly suspect. We would note that Mr. Cakalic has testified before the Tribunal on the date of 16th July, 2003, when asked about these events under oath on four different occasion, on pages 14, 17, 61, and 62, Mr. Cakalic under oath denied that this witness, and repeatedly affirmed -- that he was not beaten by this witness. So there is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The document will be marked for identification. The parties will have an opportunity to further make submissions on the admission of this document because we're now finding other sources. Mr. Jovanovic, you might have other responses to that as well. We have no time to deal with that today. You have asked the questions. It will be marked for identification. The parties will have an opportunity to make further submissions on whether or not this document should be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D3, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And it keeps that status for the time being. Thank you, Mr. Jovanovic. This concludes your testimony. Mr. Weber, could you be -- please be as short as reasonably possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Savic, you were previously asked, and this is located on page 49, line 25, through page 50, line 2, of the transcript from today. You were asked about Badza. And the question to you was: "So you think he was the assistant minister of the state security. Are you sure about that?" I believe you were nodding your head at the time. The transcript did not record a verbal response from you. Could you please answer that question.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that he was in a very high position in the Minister of the Interior. I don't know what the title of that position was. I wouldn't be sure. The fact is, however, that he had been -- that he was appointed the commander of the Territorial Defence of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: There were a number of paragraphs that were read from your statement. During the reading of these paragraphs, there were sentences that were skipped in the reading of it. I just want to confirm with you that in page 15, the third paragraph from the top, did you state in your statement of 2002: "I did not believe, and I have never seen the RSK army as a separate entity from the JNA ..." Did you also say that?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I did not understand your question. Could you repeat or rephrase.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You were --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, does this arise from cross-examination? And even if portions are read to the witness, is this a matter you could not have raised in chief?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was allowing the -- I was not objecting to counsel as he was reading the paragraphs in order to allow him to go through it, but he skipped sentences that were pertinent. And in the context of what was read to him, I believe it's unfair to let the record stand if a sentence was skipped.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I can't say that I immediately have a recollection of what was in the context of this portion being read. So in view of this explanation, I allow you to verify this with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, you were asked questions on cross-examination about segments of your 2002 statement. Do you recall those segments?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and I confirmed them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Can you confirm in your 2002 statement you also stated in the third paragraph of page 15: "I did not believe and I have never seen the RSK army as a separate entity from the JNA ..." Did you also say that in your statement?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be illogical for a non-existent state to have its army.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, my question to you was: Was that also in your statement?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it is in my statement, I adhere to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't know if we can reach some agreement maybe between the parties. I do not want to carry this witness over into next week, but there's two sentences that were not read. If we can agree to the fact that they are in the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And a question was put already whether he gave that statement in all sincerity. The portions you would like to refer to?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: It would be in the English version, page 15. It's the paragraph -- third paragraph from the top, second line, last sentence was skipped: "I do not believe, and I have never seen the RSK army as a separate entity from the JNA ..."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but why not just ask him -- apart from what you said in your statement, did you believe, or did you ever view the RSK army as an entity separate from the JNA? If you could just say yes or no to start with.
