utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'll just put it to you then. You were asked questions about the SRS in Krajina in May 1992 and read that portion of your statement. It related to Mr. Ostojic and the VRSK and the providing of weapons by them. Did you also indicate, and is this correct: "Under normal circumstances the army has the control over the army weapons, but all of a sudden these weapons were distributed through political parties and certain individuals." Is that a correct statement?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the political parties did not have the resources to be able to have weapons which to distribute. So those who had the weapons actually manipulated the weapons because no party had the resources with which to provide weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it fair to say all weapons weren't being distributed through the military?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: No, it's not fair to say that or -- could you please be clear in your answer.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not all the weapons were distributed through the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. On page 59, line 20, you were asked a question about a date in which you had a meeting with Captain Dragan. You referenced the 4th of August, 1992; however, the Prosecution notes in your proofing note you indicated the 3rd or 4th of August, 1991 --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: The witness has given his evidence. In our submission, it's not for the Prosecution to go back to his written statement to bring out an answer that they'd prefer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I earlier asked you, Mr. Weber, how this arises from cross. Is there any specific link to a portion read to the witness earlier by Mr. Jovanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: There is page 59, lines 20 through 23, this was referenced. All I'm going to put to the witness was: What is the correct date?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that something we should -- why not verify with the witness, Mr. Jordash?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Only -- I suppose I'm -- I don't have a -- I'm objecting out of principle in a way because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay, fine. Let's be very practical. I -- if a principle would obstruct us to know the exact date, then perhaps we should apply the principle in such a way that we would know about the exact date. You may ask the question, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Savic, this meeting that you had with Captain Dragan, did it occur on the 4th of August, 1992; or the 3rd or 4th of August, 1991?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When you were being interviewed in 2002, what case or what was the focus of the questions that you were asked by the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jovanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I object. In no previously given written statement of this witness is a purpose indicated to the effect for what case he's giving testimony. So this is knowledge of people who can be potential witnesses before this Court. So witnesses should not be concretely specified which case they are supposed to give testimony for so that they focus on that, so that when they give testimony in other cases they can adduce a host of other facts. The statement, in fact, does not indicate that it was given for any other case but this one. It is being used for this case. That is what I'm saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Whether that is a valid objection is another matter. What's the relevance of the question, Mr. Weber?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If -- the witness has been questioned extensively today --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So what we can -- we can ask him whether he was told. Were you told in what case your statement -- to the benefit of what Prosecution's case your statement was taken?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, he gave multiple statements. Can we just be clear --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The 2002 statement I wanted to refer to.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, it was not stated, it was not indicated.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: During the course of the interview, was there a particular accused that you were being asked questions about in 2002?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. -- the Chamber can read in the statement if you would tender it for those purposes, or you could agree with the Defence on what questions were put. What we are doing at this moment is that we are not -- this statement is not tendered into evidence, and everyone tries to get the best out of it; Mr. Jovanovic does so; you do so. That's not the way to proceed, as a matter of fact. Please proceed to your next question, and we'll finish in one or two seconds -- well, minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When you were interviewed in 2002 and 2003, was the focus either of those interviews Jovica Stanisic or Franko Simatovic?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Nothing further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Weber. We have got one minute left. Is there any urgent need to put another question to the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: No, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jovanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jovanovic, of course the Chamber would have reconsidered its decision to grant 15 minutes only if it, at the end, would have considered it to be unfair. What happened is that the joint Defence assured the Chamber that we would conclude the evidence of this witness today. And then suddenly, although the Chamber could personally observe that there was communication and apparently consultation between the Defence teams, was confronted at a very late stage with a conclusion that we could not -- that you could not finish your testimony today. That was at a time when the Defence had taken already two hours and 46 minutes I think. The OTP had taken two hours and nine minutes. The guidance of the Chamber was that the parties would get I think it was 80 to 100 per cent of the time in chief, which would mean a little bit less than two hours. Now, you got approximately 50 per cent of a little bit less than two hours. The Chamber has further allowed you to conduct cross-examination in a rather extraordinary way which gave you the advantage of obtaining -- of having in evidence quite a bit more than you would under normal circumstances have obtained. At the same time, I announce to the parties that the way in which we proceeded today is not the way we are going to proceed in the days and months -- days, weeks, and months to come. Whether we'll deal with this in open court or whether the parties will be invited soon to further discuss what we expect, for example, division of time between the Defence teams. If you can't agree on it, fine, the Chamber will just say 50 per cent for you, 50 per cent for you, but not the way in which it was done. Another observation is, Mr. Jovanovic, there would have been technical different ways of having into evidence certain portions of the statement that should have been properly prepared. We could have seen whether it would have been possible to have admitted portions of the statement under Rule 92 ter. But reading here and having everyone out of breath after 15 minutes is not the way in which we'll proceed. At this moment, Mr. Savic, I would like to thank you very much for coming to The Hague because it ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I said I would like to thank you very much for coming to The Hague because matters have not changed since my last consultation with my colleagues, that the Bench has no further questions for you. I wish you a safe trip home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Therefore, we adjourn for the day, and we'll resume on Wednesday, the 15th of July, in Courtroom I, at a quarter past 2.00 in the afternoon. We stand adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 15th day of July, 2009, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.15 p.m.,
